KSI-CED-RAT.name: Reviewing All Training
KSI-CED-RAT.statement: The effectiveness of relevant cybersecurity education and training is persistently reviewed, including at least general training for all employees, role-specific training for employees in high risk roles, training for development and engineering staff on secure software delivery, and training for staff involved with incident response or disaster recovery.

KSI-CMT-LMC.name: Logging Changes
KSI-CMT-LMC.statement: Modifications to the cloud service offering are logged and monitored.

KSI-CMT-RMV.name: Redeploying vs Modifying
KSI-CMT-RMV.statement: Changes to machine-based information resources are executed through the redeployment of version controlled resources rather than direct modification wherever reasonable.

KSI-CMT-RVP.name: Reviewing Change Procedures
KSI-CMT-RVP.statement: The effectiveness of documented change management procedures is persistently reviewed.

KSI-CMT-VTD.name: Validating Throughout Deployment
KSI-CMT-VTD.statement: Persistent testing and validation of changes throughout deployment is automated.

KSI-CNA-DFP.name: Defining Functionality and Privileges
KSI-CNA-DFP.statement: The functionality and privileges for infrastructure and services are strictly defined.

KSI-CNA-EIS.name: Enforcing Intended State
KSI-CNA-EIS.statement: Automated services are used to persistently assess the security of all machine-based information resources and automatically enforce their intended operational state.

KSI-CNA-IBP.name: Implementing Best Practices
KSI-CNA-IBP.statement: The use and configuration of third-party machine-based information resources is persistently compared against the original provider's best practices and guidance.

KSI-CNA-MAT.name: Minimizing Attack Surface
KSI-CNA-MAT.statement: Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they have a minimal attack surface and that lateral movement is minimized if compromised.

KSI-CNA-OFA.name: Optimizing for Availability
KSI-CNA-OFA.statement: Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they are appropriately optimized for high availability and rapid recovery.

KSI-CNA-RNT.name: Restricting Network Traffic
KSI-CNA-RNT.statement: Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they are appropriately configured to limit inbound and outbound network traffic.

KSI-CNA-RVP.name: Reviewing Protections
KSI-CNA-RVP.statement: The effectiveness of protection against denial of service attacks and other unwanted activity for machine-based information resources is persistently reviewed.

KSI-CNA-ULN.name: Using Logical Networking
KSI-CNA-ULN.statement: Logical networking and related capabilities are used and persistently reviewed to enforce traffic flow controls.

KSI-IAM-AAM.name: Automating Account Management
KSI-IAM-AAM.statement: The lifecycle and privileges of all accounts, roles, and groups are securely managed using automation.

KSI-IAM-APM.name: Adopting Passwordless Methods
KSI-IAM-APM.statement: Secure passwordless methods are used for user authentication and authorization when feasible, otherwise strong passwords with phishing-resistant MFA is used.

KSI-IAM-ELP.name: Ensuring Least Privilege
KSI-IAM-ELP.statement: Identity and access management measures are used and persistently reviewed to ensure each user or device can only access the resources they need.

KSI-IAM-JIT.name: Authorizing Just-in-Time
KSI-IAM-JIT.statement: A least-privileged, role and attribute-based, and just-in-time security authorization model is used and persistently reviewed for all user and non-user accounts and services.

KSI-IAM-SNU.name: Securing Non-User Authentication
KSI-IAM-SNU.statement: Appropriately secure authentication methods are used and persistently reviewed for non-user accounts and services.

KSI-IAM-SUS.name: Responding to Suspicious Activity
KSI-IAM-SUS.statement: Accounts with privileged access are disabled or otherwise secured in response to suspicious activity.

KSI-INR-AAR.name: Generating After Action Reports
KSI-INR-AAR.statement: Incident after action reports are generated and lessons learned are persistently incorporated.

KSI-INR-RIR.name: Reviewing Incident Response Procedures
KSI-INR-RIR.statement: The effectiveness of documented incident response procedures is persistently reviewed.

KSI-INR-RPI.name: Reviewing Past Incidents
KSI-INR-RPI.statement: Past incidents are persistently reviewed for patterns or vulnerabilities that were not previously apparent or identified.

KSI-MLA-ALA.name: Authorizing Log Access
KSI-MLA-ALA.statement: A least-privileged, role and attribute-based, and just-in-time access authorization model is used and persistently reviewed for access to log data based on organizationally defined data sensitivity.

KSI-MLA-EVC.name: Evaluating Configurations
KSI-MLA-EVC.statement: The configuration of machine-based information resources, especially infrastructure as code, is persistently evaluated and tested.

KSI-MLA-LET.name: Logging Event Types
KSI-MLA-LET.statement: A list of information resources and event types that will be logged, monitored, and audited is maintained and persistently reviewed to ensure these activities occur.

KSI-MLA-OSM.name: Operating SIEM Capability
KSI-MLA-OSM.statement: A Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) or similar system(s) is used and persistently reviewed for centralized, tamper-resistant logging of events, activities, and changes.

KSI-MLA-RVL.name: Reviewing Logs
KSI-MLA-RVL.statement: Logs are persistently reviewed and audited.

KSI-PIY-GIV.name: Generating Inventories
KSI-PIY-GIV.statement: Authoritative sources are used to automatically generate real-time inventories of all information resources when needed.

KSI-PIY-RES.name: Reviewing Executive Support
KSI-PIY-RES.statement: Executive support for achieving the provider's security goals is persistently reviewed and demonstrated.

KSI-PIY-RIS.name: Reviewing Investments in Security
KSI-PIY-RIS.statement: The effectiveness of the provider's investments in achieving security goals is persistently reviewed.

KSI-PIY-RSD.name: Reviewing Security in the SDLC
KSI-PIY-RSD.statement: The effectiveness of building security and privacy considerations into the Software Development Lifecycle and aligning with CISA Secure By Design principles is persistently reviewed.

KSI-PIY-RVD.name: Reviewing Vulnerability Disclosures
KSI-PIY-RVD.statement: The effectiveness of the provider's vulnerability disclosure program is persistently reviewed.

KSI-RPL-ABO.name: Aligning Backups with Objectives
KSI-RPL-ABO.statement: The alignment of machine-based information resource backups with defined recovery objectives is persistently reviewed.

KSI-RPL-ARP.name: Aligning Recovery Plan
KSI-RPL-ARP.statement: The alignment of recovery plans with defined recovery objectives is persistently reviewed.

KSI-RPL-RRO.name: Reviewing Recovery Objectives
KSI-RPL-RRO.statement: The desired Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) are defined and persistently reviewed for alignment with the provider's business needs and capabilities.

KSI-RPL-TRC.name: Testing Recovery Capabilities
KSI-RPL-TRC.statement: The capability to recover from incidents and contingencies aligned with defined recovery objectives is persistently tested.

KSI-SCR-MIT.name: Mitigating Supply Chain Risk
KSI-SCR-MIT.statement: Persistently identify, review, and mitigate potential supply chain risks.

KSI-SCR-MON.name: Monitoring Supply Chain Risk
KSI-SCR-MON.statement: Third party software information resources are automatically monitored for upstream vulnerabilities using mechanisms that may include contractual notification requirements or active monitoring services.

KSI-SVC-ACM.name: Automating Configuration Management
KSI-SVC-ACM.statement: The configuration of machine-based information resources is managed using automation and persistently reviewed for drift.

KSI-SVC-ASM.name: Automating Secret Management
KSI-SVC-ASM.statement: Management, protection, and regular rotation of digital keys, certificates, and other secrets is automated and persistently reviewed.

KSI-SVC-EIS.name: Evaluating and Improving Security
KSI-SVC-EIS.statement: Information resources are persistently evaluated for opportunities to improve security and those improvements are persistently made.

KSI-SVC-PRR.name: Preventing Residual Risk
KSI-SVC-PRR.statement: Plans, procedures, and the state of information resources are persistently reviewed after making changes to limit and remove unwanted residual elements that would likely negatively affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of federal customer data.

KSI-SVC-RUD.name: Removing Unwanted Data
KSI-SVC-RUD.statement: Unwanted federal customer data is removed promptly when requested by an agency in alignment with customer agreements, including from backups if appropriate; this typically applies when a customer spills information or when a customer seeks to remove information from a service due to a change in usage.

KSI-SVC-SIN.name: Securing Information
KSI-SVC-SIN.statement: Information is encrypted or otherwise secured from unwanted access or modification.

KSI-SVC-VCM.name: Validating Communications
KSI-SVC-VCM.statement: The authenticity and integrity of communications between machine-based information resources is persistently validated using automation.

KSI-SVC-VRI.name: Validating Resource Integrity
KSI-SVC-VRI.statement: Use cryptographic methods to validate the integrity of machine-based information resources.

MAS-CSO-IIR.name: Identify Information Resources
MAS-CSO-IIR.statement: Providers MUST identify a set of information resources to assess for FedRAMP Certification that includes all information resources that are likely to handle federal customer data or likely to impact the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of federal customer data handled by the cloud service offering; this set of information resources is the cloud service offering.

SCN-CSO-EVA.name: Evaluate Changes
SCN-CSO-EVA.statement: Providers MUST evaluate all potential significant changes to determine the type of significant change and follow the appropriate Significant Change Notification rules.

VDR-CSO-DET.name: Vulnerability Detection
VDR-CSO-DET.statement: Providers MUST systematically, persistently, and promptly discover and identify vulnerabilities within their cloud service offering using appropriate techniques such as assessment, scanning, threat intelligence, vulnerability disclosure mechanisms, bug bounties, penetration testing, incident response, automated control testing, supply chain monitoring, and other relevant capabilities; this process is called vulnerability detection. Vulnerability detection includes persistently verifying and validating that information resources and processes are operating as intended and documented for FedRAMP Practices.

VDR-TFR-PDD.name: Persistent Drift Detection
VDR-TFR-PDD.statement: Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD persistently perform vulnerability detection on all information resources that are likely to drift, at least once every 14 days.

VDR-TFR-PVR.name: Mitigation and Remediation Expectations
